notes.title: Minor bug fixes
notes.notes:
[p]Hello -

A very small update, but it smooths out a few rough edges and clears up some confusion:[/p][list][*][p]Hammer can no longer break the computer. That was never the intended behavior, and it should now function as originally designed.[/p][/*][*][p]Added a “Are you sure you want to quit?” dialog to prevent accidental exits.[/p][/*][*][p]Pressing ESC now cleanly exits the computer interface. This should feel more natural and intuitive. [/p][/*][/list][p]Thank you, once again, for playing and sharing Hellkind. Even a tiny patch like this comes from paying attention to the way you’re experiencing the game. Every bug report, suggestion, and kind message matters.[/p][p][/p][p][i]From the terminal.[/i][/p][p]Emir Arkman / Motamot[/p]

notes.title: Fixes - And a Personal Thank You!
notes.notes:
[p][b][i]Update: July 5, 2025[/i][/b][/p][p]
First of all thank you, truly, for playing Hellkind. This project was made quietly, in the late hours, with deep love for folklore, atmosphere, and storytelling. I never expected the kind of warmth and encouragement that’s come since release, and every message, kind word, screenshot, video, stream and any kind of support has meant more than I can say.
[/p][p]A small update has just been released with a handful of tweaks and fixes, aimed at improving the experience:
[/p][list][*][p]Volume adjustments: Several sounds in the game have been adjusted and more 3D sounds added.[/p][/*][*][p]Input handling: Player hammer control are now correctly paused when the character is invisible.[/p][/*][*][p]Refined wording: Several pieces of ingame text have been slightly adjusted to improve clarity and flow. These are super minor changes.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed the empty prompt bug: A bug where the bottom prompt would sometimes open with an empty box has been fixed.[/p][/*][*][p]Steam Deck preparations: Made some adjustments to better support the Steam Deck in the future. This doesn’t change anything visible yet, but it lays the foundation for a smoother experience on the device in the near future. Especially the keyboard input part.[/p][/*][/list][p][/p][p]Seeing people explore this strange little world and connect with it in their own way has been a quiet dream come true. I’m incredibly grateful.
[/p][p]Thank you,[/p][p]Emir Arkman / Motamot[/p]
